chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: There is no manumission for the believer after death.
And no recompense (for deeds) after death.

key_terms.النَّصْلُ: Recompense or offspring (deeds continuing after death)

ai.seo_question: What happens to a person's good deeds and manumission after they die in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s clarification that manumission is an immediate act of ownership transfer effective upon the master's declaration, thus becoming part of the estate rather than a posthumous bequest. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of *fard* (obligatory execution) for certain acts, distinguishing them from *wasiyya* (bequest), and highlights the finality of individual accountability where deeds cease to accrue new merit for the deceased, though their legacy may benefit others through ongoing charity (*sadaqah jariyah*).
